title: [DRAFT] XR: Clean up cached OpenGL FBOs when native textures are freed

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
I started looking into this due to log messages on Android XR about swapchain images not being freed because the reference count was greater than 1 (see below).

I haven't managed to fix that, and I'm not even 100% sure that it's caused by anything Godot is doing, but looking into that led me to realize that we are caching OpenGL FBOs for the swapchain images, and never freeing them (unless the app switches from XR to non-XR mode, which not all XR interfaces can even do). And, in fact, on Android we weren't even correctly freeing them when the app shutdown, because we no longer had a current EGL context.

So, what this PR does:

- Allows freeing textures that are used as render targets _if_ they come from a native handle. The lifetime of these textures is controlled outside of Godot, and we need to be able to free them when the external owner says they are no longer valid
  - And freeing a texture which is used on a cached FBO will lead to that FBO to be deleted!
- ~~Fixes some issues with `render_target_create`: it wasn't setting `RenderTarget::self` and the pointer on `Texture::render_target` was incorrect (it was a pointer to a struct on the stack, not the struct in `render_target_owner`)~~
- ~~Correctly unbinds textures when we are using a `TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY` (rather than `TEXTURE_2D`) as we do in XR. (I thought maybe that lingering bind was the cause of the reference; it wasn't, but this change is still correct.)~~
- ~~On Android, makes the EGL surface current before doing shutdown, so our OpenGL calls to free various resources will actually work~~

**UPDATE (2026-08-24):** The changes from points nr 2, 3, and 4 were moved to:
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122271
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/122269

## Original log messages

On an Android XR headset, I noticed these messages in `adb logcat`:

```
07-29 13:20:14.277 17665 17720 E godot   : ERROR: Condition "t->is_render_target" is true.
07-29 13:20:14.277 17665 17720 E godot   :    at: texture_free (drivers/gles3/storage/texture_storage.cpp:1004) 
07-29 13:20:14.277 17665 17720 E godot   : ERROR: Condition "t->is_render_target" is true.
07-29 13:20:14.277 17665 17720 E godot   :    at: texture_free (drivers/gles3/storage/texture_storage.cpp:1004)
07-29 13:20:14.277 17665 17720 E godot   : ERROR: Condition "t->is_render_target" is true.
07-29 13:20:14.277 17665 17720 E godot   :    at: texture_free (drivers/gles3/storage/texture_storage.cpp:1004)
07-29 13:20:14.277 17665 17720 E godot   : ERROR: Condition "t->is_render_target" is true.
07-29 13:20:14.277 17665 17720 E godot   :    at: texture_free (drivers/gles3/storage/texture_storage.cpp:1004)
07-29 13:20:14.277 17665 17720 W as.may.moat: Swapchain image buffer reference count is not 1 before final release; this means that the app is holding on to the buffer and the buffer will likely leak; image index: 0, reference count: 3
07-29 13:20:14.277 17665 17720 W as.may.moat: Swapchain image buffer reference count is not 1 before final release; this means that the app is holding on to the buffer and the buffer will likely leak; image index: 1, reference count: 3
07-29 13:20:14.277 17665 17720 W as.may.moat: Swapchain image buffer reference count is not 1 before final release; this means that the app is holding on to the buffer and the buffer will likely leak; image index: 2, reference count: 3
07-29 13:20:14.277 17665 17720 W as.may.moat: Swapchain image buffer reference count is not 1 before final release; this means that the app is holding on to the buffer and the buffer will likely leak; image index: 3, reference count: 3
```

This PR does fix the `ERROR: Condition "t->is_render_target" is true` errors, and now cleans those textures up correctly.

But it still doesn't fix the `Swapchain image buffer reference count is not 1 before final release` errors, which imply that we may be leaking these textures. I haven't found anything yet that will get rid of those. (But, again, I'm not 100% sure there even is anything we're doing wrong that's leading to that error.)
